([[Saint Paul, Minnesota]]) | college = [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]] (2018–2020) | highlights = * Third-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] – [[Sporting News|SN]] ([[2020 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2020]]) * Second-team All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] (2020) * Big Ten All-Defensive Team (2020) * [[Nike Hoop Summit]] (2018) | medal_templates = }} '''Akinfayoshe Daniel Oturu''' (born September 20, 1999) is a Nigerian-American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota Golden Gophers]]. ==High school career== Oturu played basketball for [[Cretin-Derham Hall High School]] in [[Saint Paul, Minnesota]] for four years. He grew from 6'6 as a freshman to 6'9 as a junior and developed good hand-eye coordination and navigation on the court. As a senior, he averaged 18.8 points, 11.5 rebounds and 6.1 blocks per game and became his school's all-time leader in each of the three categories.{{cite web |last1=Mizutani |first1=Dane |title=CDH’s Daniel Oturu shines on and off court |url=https://www.twincities.com/2018/03/20/cretin-derham-hall-star-daniel-oturu-shines-bright-on-and-off-the-court/ |website=[[St. Paul Pioneer Press]] |accessdate=January 8, 2020 |date=March 20, 2018}} In his final season, Oturu led his team to a Class 4A state championship over [[Apple Valley High School (Minnesota)|Apple Valley High School]], scoring a game-winning [[slam dunk|dunk]] with 0.5 seconds left in regulation. Despite his strong play, he was excluded from the all-tournament team for sportsmanship reasons, as he had received a [[technical foul]] for shoving opposing player, [[Tre Jones]], in the first half.{{cite web |last1=Rand |first1=Michael |title='Sportsmanship' kept dominant Oturu off boys' basketball all-tournament team |url=http://www.startribune.com/why-wasnt-cretin-star-daniel-oturu-on-the-boys-basketball-all-tournament-team/477939563/ |website=[[Star Tribune]] |accessdate=January 8, 2020 |date=March 26, 2018}} Oturu was invited to play for the World Select team, representing his parents' home country of Nigeria, at the [[Nike Hoop Summit]] in [[Portland, Oregon]].{{cite web |last1=Fuller |first1=Marcus |title=Gophers recruit Daniel Oturu makes Nike Summit World Select team |url=http://www.startribune.com/gophers-recruit-daniel-oturu-makes-nike-summit-world-select-team/478696873/ |website=[[Star Tribune]] |accessdate=January 8, 2020 |date=April 3, 2018}} He was considered a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]] over offers from [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], among others.{{cite web |last1=Owen |first1=Dan |title=2018 PF Daniel Oturu Commits to Gophers |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/breaking-2018-pf-daniel-oturu-commits-to-gophers/ |website=[[CBSSports.com]] |accessdate=January 8, 2020 |date=January 19, 2017}} ==College career== Oturu had shoulder surgery prior to his freshman season. On December 24, 2018, Oturu was named [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] freshman of the week after scoring 20 points and pulling down 11 rebounds in a 86–67 win over [[North Carolina A&T Aggies men's basketball|North Carolina A&T]].{{cite news |last1=Fuller |first1=Marcus |title=Gophers center Daniel Oturu named Big Ten freshman of the week |url=http://www.startribune.com/gophers-center-daniel-oturu-named-big-ten-freshman-of-the-week/503450332/ |accessdate=January 16, 2020 |work=[[Star Tribune]] |date=December 24, 2019}} He tied his season-high of 20 points in a 68–64 loss to [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]] on February 24, 2019.{{cite news |title=Mathis scores 18 to help Rutgers beat Minnesota 68–64 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401082509 |accessdate=January 16, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 24, 2019}} Despite Oturu's strong play, he was not named in the Big Ten Freshman Team, which he cited as motivation.{{cite news |last1=Fuller |first1=Marcus |title=Gophers' Daniel Oturu motivated by not making All-Big Ten freshman team |url=http://www.startribune.com/gophers-daniel-oturu-motivated-by-not-making-all-big-ten-freshman-team/507054462/ |accessdate=January 16, 2020 |work=[[Star Tribune]] |date=March 12, 2019}} Oturu averaged 10.8 points per game and led Big Ten freshman in rebounding with 7.0 per game, blocked shots with 46, and field goal percentage with 55 percent. In the offseason, Oturu worked on bulking up to help replace the loss of [[Jordan Murphy (basketball)|Jordan Murphy]].{{cite news |last1=Fuller |first1=Marcus |url=http://www.startribune.com/gophers-center-daniel-oturu-returns-bigger-and-better/561286562/ |title=Richard Pitino wants bigger Oturu to be more physical, shoot some threes |accessdate=January 16, 2020 |work=[[Star Tribune]] |date=September 25, 2019}} During his sophomore season he was named Big Ten player of the week on December 30, after posting 21 points and a career-high 20 rebounds in an 89–62 win against [[Florida International Panthers men's basketball|Florida International]], shooting 8-of-12 from the floor.{{Cite web|url=http://bigten.org/news/2019/12/30/illinois-and-minnesota-claim-weekly-mens-basketball-honors.aspx|title=Illinois and Minnesota Claim Weekly Men’s Basketball Honors|website=[[Big Ten Conference]]|date=December 30, 2019|access-date=January 16, 2020}} On January 12, 2020, Oturu scored a career-high 30 points in a 75–67 upset of [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] despite playing with a shoulder injury.{{cite news |title=Oturu scores 30 as Minnesota beats No. 19 Michigan 75–67 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166166 |accessdate=January 16, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 12, 2020}} He was named Big Ten Player of the Week on January 13.{{Cite web|url=http://bigten.org/news/2020/1/13/illinois-minnesota-and-purdue-claim-weekly-mens-basketball-honors.aspx|title=Illinois, Minnesota and Purdue Claim Weekly Men’s Basketball Honors|website=[[Big life== Both of Oturu's parents are natives of [[Nigeria]]. His mother, Deborah, is from [[Ife]] and his father, Francis, is from Fadeyi, a suburb of [[Lagos]].{{cite web |last1=Fuller |first1=Marcus |title=For Gophers basketball player Daniel Oturu, home is where the heart is |url=http://www.startribune.com/for-gophers-basketball-player-daniel-oturu-home-is-where-the-heart-is/564290832/ |website=[[Star Tribune]] |accessdate=January 7, 2020 |date=November 3, 2019}} Francis played [[table tennis]] for the Nigerian national team and moved to the United States because of his table tennis career. Oturu has an older sister, Eunice.{{cite web |last1=Greder |first1=Andy |title=Gophers: Before basketball in Woodbury, Oturus were playing ping pong in Nigeria |url=https://www.twincities.com/2019/02/20/gophers-before-basketball-in-woodbury-oturus-were-playing-ping-pong-in-nigeria/ |website=[[St. Paul Pioneer Press]] |accessdate=January 7, 2020 |date=February 4, 2019}} Oturu was given his middle name, Daniel, by his mother, who viewed it as a strong [[Bible|biblical]] name. His first name, Akinfayoshe, combines the [[Yoruba language|Yoruba]] words "Akin" (hero) and "fayoshe" (joy and happiness). Oturu comes from a [[Christians|Christian]] family. Both of his parents are [[Minister (Christianity)|ministers]] at a branch of the [[Mountain of Fire and Miracles Ministries]] in [[Saint Paul, Minnesota]].
